observer: Codex; user confirmed browsers and moving video/game content

environment.client: desktop_web; browser versions and hardware unknown
environment.source: Private Tempo media.sample spans and production host/container metrics via authorized SSH
environment.mutations: None; no restart, deployment, media recording or load generation

findings: Initial profile captures 2560x1440 at 60fps and only sets publishing bitrate/FPS. Resolution scaling exists in updateScreenShareProfile but is absent on initial start. Receiver dimensions confirm 1440p under a 1080p target.
For moving content the high-resolution path is not consistently smooth; later sender and receiver report similarly low FPS. Exact cause needs per-layer active/quality-limitation/capture diagnostics.
Host resource samples show no server CPU or RAM saturation; this does not exclude client or path bottlenecks.
HTML audio is forced unmuted at volume 1 by WebAudioGain, leaving mute/volume solely to GainNode. A native output safeguard needs regression coverage and live acceptance.
Prometheus does not scrape API media histograms. Latest admin samples overwrite other clients of the same platform/direction. Detailed per-client samples are available in Tempo.
limitations: No visual inspection or listening: browser connector returned Unable to load browser request-header policy on retries. Image sharpness, A/V sync and perceived delay were not measured.
Client diagnostics are self-reported, sparse and visibility-dependent; report means are not time-weighted. Missing receiver reports do not prove disconnect or freeze.
Sender selects the largest reported simulcast layer; bitrate totals all layers. Do not compare sender bitrate directly with one receiver or treat a dimension switch as capture resizing.
One presented-FPS value of 102.5 for a 30fps target suggests a sampling/counter artefact; prefer decoded FPS and medians. Zero-FPS states alone do not measure freeze duration.
The later window uses a 60fps target and four connection clients; it is not an unchanged continuation of the original three-client 30fps scenario.
No codec, QP, keyframe, decoder load, jitter-buffer delay or end-to-end latency was recorded. QA-06/QA-07 and capacity gates remain open.
privacy: Only anonymous aggregates saved in Git; no account/session IDs, names, tokens, SDP, ICE addresses or media payloads.
